# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Supporting design document**. This document supports
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) by
> expanding the RFC’s phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase sequence and acceptance gates in the main body of RFC-039 are the sole authority. This
> document is responsible only for decomposing the work to an executable granularity and registering
> conflicts that have not yet been adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one to the phase sequence in RFC-039                               |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each able to form and archive an independent team |
| **Level 3** | 262         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                     |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the history of this document has **zero
occurrences** of the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` (this can be verified with
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no references
anywhere else in the repository. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that phase has been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so the numbering in P8 is
aligned with its phase number (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for the tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
rationale for the phase sequence (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered level-2/level-3 rows **must
contain two fields**—“**Owning Phase**” (the P phase to which the task truly belongs, which may
differ from the containing section) and “**Blocks Mainline**”. `Pending scheduling` is no longer the
default state; an unmarked task is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique across
the entire document** (tasks in cross-track work use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must
not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable)—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining Pattern-Matching Completion Work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not
write the fix, the criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short hash>`). This table is a
tracker, not a process chronicle. **Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**:
phrases such as “user decision A/B/C,” “option A,” or “the final implementation is…” do not belong
in this table. The tracker answers only “is it complete?”; consult the commit message and the
decision registry in RFC-039 for adjudications and results.

**The short hash is authoritative after the push**: a closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push is complete. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see “Obtain the commit hash after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself does not carry a
hash—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains only numbers**: the level-1/2/3 counts under `Positioning and Scope`
contain only current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …` does not belong in the
table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Resolution                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC defines P5 (checker decomposition) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform the decomposition; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one `annotations.rs` entry, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                          | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                 |
| G2  | **All three `include!` refactoring locations lack ownership and implementation**. RFC lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; S7 in `06` also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) **does not contain `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                                        | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC and 06 now point here                  |
| G3  | **Three concurrent inventories of CI scripts exist**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists another 4 checks (all with different names); `04` previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified inventory**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership under P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified inventory (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to that table               |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it and the `Precedence` enum “must be deleted together”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                                      | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer removed)                                                                      |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 objective**: RFC and the index in this directory previously said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | It has been consolidated into **a declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent constructs / do not engage in
endless filling / do not patch something that should be refactored) constrain every action in
P1–P10. The rules must be established before work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives tests, work
will already start adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4
conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Approach)

Source: vulnerability-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 ＋
**2026-10-07 silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Routing of semantic corrections (D59, decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a subsequent
> phase discovers a defect where “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and uncontrolled resources** (crashes, stack exhaustion,
> silently incorrect answers)—it **may be fixed along the refactoring path**, but all four
> conditions are mandatory: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must exist first and must
> genuinely be red); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously
> compiled successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing
> diagnostic codes/text/exit codes must not be removed or modified); ③ register it in the same
> commit (this row records the error type + a revision note for that phase + the PR required block’s
> “Error Type” line); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D
> user-visible semantics / E external contract table / F RFC-level design changes must still be
> adjudicated first.** See [07 §Criteria for Routing Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md)
> for the expanded criteria and A–F allowlist; **the “default super-refactoring + retroactive
> registration” approach is not adopted** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion,
> there is no way to distinguish a fix from a regression, and it conflicts with both “C5′ does not
> exist” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

**Acceptance**: the vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fixes must
turn them red again**. **Risk**: adding E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and P9’s 9.2 gate as the criteria. **Risk**: the new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus differential baselines
and a CHANGELOG update.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 does not have to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness vulnerabilities
> (`Sorted(3)` silently passing) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3
> (convert panic to diagnostic) has no prerequisites and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by
an ordering constraint**; it is separate from P10 S5 “lower the visibility of `pub` items”
(narrowing Rust `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed in full before P4**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the rewriting
surfaces of all four refactoring phases; reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST Dead Variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                          |
| The `pub` branches of `auto_bind_to_type` and `collect_exports`     | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!` → real `mod` and checker decomposition are **pure moves**, and the `pub` branches will be moved verbatim into the new files)                                                                                                           |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside the `check_project` body)                        | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| The `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                          | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must have a red criterion before code is
   changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced top-level
   binding in a Lib/Script role newly reports W1001 (previously public items were always exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case and `is_pub` fixture
   from `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs`, equivalent new cases must replace them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (a new parse error + a new W1001) ⇒
   update the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to be zero-diff, and any non-zero difference must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the whole batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed with
   other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` must all be green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with 3.4 at the file level (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must
be serial and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track must precede P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g
track does not depend on 3.4; the implementer decides which to do first based on the work in hand.

> **Commit comparison (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint rows) and RFC-039 D56 were merged into `97071c81b` while the parallel-flow
> sweep cleaned the workspace—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary registration + landing
> D57/D58 decisions,” without mentioning this track. History is not rewritten; following the
> existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note), it is registered in place
> as a retrospective bisect marker.

|                                                  | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with **named arguments** loses its formal-parameter name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure): calling a cross-unit (registry-injected) method with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` has `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: class C** (old behavior was not success: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by runtime failure or a silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two rounds of narrowing on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—retrieve the declaration-time formal names from the unique cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` using the defining unit’s qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (the candidate ↔ mixed IR name ↔ formal name vectors are in the same order as in the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table, rather than using two separate bare names. These two locations fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments on alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “the same input yields multiple results” caused by HashMap iteration order**; this is not a fix for the original bug; the criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed per method key; removing the ascending merge produces two results). **Criterion (red before green)**: two driver-level tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare-import single candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name, 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header marks the failure-history gate); unit test in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (`method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None, positive control returns a non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the deterministic criterion above). Project-level fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); corpus differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (the intermediate state once contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`, `alias-overload` never entered final history). The line-count change = an inevitable result of fixtures entering and leaving (after `corpus_probe` regeneration, it is byte-for-byte identical to the checked-in baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known Gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② should have reported but did not, class A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / builtin container constructors other than `len` with named arguments / whole-module imports / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these are corrected based on P0 measurements**: ① **static-function forms** (both same-unit and cross-unit, definition form and binding form) are **entirely unavailable today**—same-unit `check` reports E3006, cross-unit definition-form `run` reports E6007, and cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments report the same code, so this is unrelated to named arguments and is not “named arguments being silently discarded”; ② **positional arguments on RFC-004 cross-unit calls also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), because the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table, which is likewise unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, incidental D59 class A fix: old behavior E6007/E1014 was not success, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **named arguments on alias imports** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These previously produced runtime E6007 from silently dropped arguments and check-time `E1014 (available: )` false rejections, respectively, and now all bind by declaration-time formal name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file’s header). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one of which is closed: a same-named type in the current unit + an alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the local declaration) **has been closed with 4.9.10-S2a’s import-surface consolidation** (project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is fully green); the remaining one is: function-body-level / cross-scope imports are merged globally by unit (shared import table)—this form does not work in the first place (an existing defect: check passes, run reports E6006), was not introduced by this batch, and remains unfixed. **Deleted in this round (relative to the first six rounds of 4.9.9)**: candidate-provider priority, candidate-signature comparison, owner/compatibility inference, the `frontend::module::import_face` shared-provider table, the IR-side “no name table ⇒ E1014” fallback, and the **E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution points**—the latter rejects mixed / alias-only forms that previously ran on the parent commit (class D), and the 2026-11-26 decision withdrew it; this round introduces no new ambiguity determination. **Visible changes**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (**bare-name imports**, including two-candidate overloads) change from E1014 with an empty table to binding by name (measured 6.0 / 30); ② all other forms return to pre-4.9.9 behavior (named arguments are silently ignored or discarded, see “Known Gaps”); ③ a single method binding no longer varies with HashMap iteration order for the same input (class C). **Status**: completed on 2026-11-26 (including the narrowing round and review pass). | 4.9.7         | See the criteria in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` and `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs` (the latter added with 4.9.10-S2b), and `src/frontend/module/registry.rs`; root-cause fix in 4.9.10                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                  | 4.9.10 Cross-unit method identity is undefined (registered 2026-11-25, structural issue confirmed during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not include module qualification, so for same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`driver::arms::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each guess the provider by name, and changing any one of them moves the “silent wrong value” to another location. **Root-cause solution**: upgrade type identity to **module-qualified identity** (`{module}.{Type}`), and change the method-candidate key accordingly to `{module}.{Type}.{method}`; one resolver produces it and the three locations only read it. This requires changing the shape of the `overload_resolutions` key and mixed IR names; D59 **class D** (requires adjudication). **Disposition in this round (after two rounds of narrowing following 4.9.9)**: 4.9.9 **introduces no new rejection**—the class-D rejection list from the first six rounds (all named arguments ⇒ E1014 / conflicting positional-argument forms ⇒ E1107 / E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution points) is deleted along with the mechanism, and all of it is void; import forms and positional arguments for mixed / alias-only / conflicting forms that ran on the parent commit are restored. **Residual surface (after this round closes)**: ① function-body-level / cross-scope imports are merged globally by unit (shared import table), and this form does not work in the first place (existing defect: check passes, run reports E6006); ② named arguments are still silently ignored or discarded in these forms (D60② class A): **static-function forms** (same-unit `check` E3006; cross-unit definition-form `run` E6007; cross-unit binding-form `run` E6006—positional and named arguments report the same code, so this is unrelated to named arguments), **RFC-004 cross-unit** (positional arguments also report E6006), **closure-value binding**, **block-body function declaration**, and **builtin containers other than `len`** (forms such as `size`: named arguments are ignored, `length` is 0, and runtime reports E6005; the `len` form works normally). **Three items closed with this round**: ① method-candidate key / method key changed to module-qualified `{module}.{Type}.{method}` (L0’s dual `DefPath` representation + S2a’s table key and single-point resolution; all three consumers named at registration time—`visible_method_overloads`, formal-name reverse lookup `method_param_info`, and `method_dispatch_name`—have been deleted); ② a same-named type in the current unit + an alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist); ③ named arguments in alias imports / the namespace arm / the inferred receiver (three forms turn green, see the corresponding section of 4.9.9). **L3 type-identity residual (migration surface, unfixed; was red at L0 and is not a regression from this round)**: ① the type name itself is still not module-qualified—the static type name in `MonoType` is the **definition-side bare name**, so same-named types across units cannot be distinguished at the type layer and can only be worked around using the import surface + binding identity; ② `VarInfo::type_identity` covers only **local-binding registration points** (written annotation / constructor write path), and **formals, pattern bindings, closure formals, and `for` variables** are not registered—at these locations, the receiver can still be resolved only by static type name (`set_type_identity` has only one call site across the repository). **Status**: implemented (L0 / S1 / **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is migrated with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; measurement
shows that 5.3 did **not** migrate it, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only decompose blocks that are confirmed to be large.** Do not split modules of only 200–400
lines—this increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides no decoupling benefit. The
remaining submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) will be split when their files grow back to
1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (first-principles rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: the end state of D62 is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions
> share one set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **only input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual-argument
> view and implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a
> **pure decision** (identical after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals / value environment /
> single-value pinning / Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (and holds for
> both closed and open/recursive forms); Σ’s constructor points **reuse the same evidence
> interface** rather than establishing another one. **The completion criterion = the invariant
> holds, not that the names of the subphases have run.**

> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 adjudication → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require

> depend on 6.9.3’s typed exit. **P7 gate = A/B/C exits; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisites: F4 adjudication (A adjudicated, 2026-11-16; measurement)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter the request” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have
> been deleted; the current mechanism is that an open item’s `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no
> request is created, and the representation layer’s `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold
> `k-1`. **The decision is changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open items enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1, restoring the second field from IR, breaks the
> single representation/evaluator, and C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing pushes the
> recursive chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a: conditionally fold within the instance /
> T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original at the boundary / T-c: a termination layer or
> specification change). **Measure first, then adjudicate; before measurement, “A is implementable”
> must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b,
> bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and complete I4 is not claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “the decision point follows the unified path first; after unified failure, equivalence may be
> used, but all partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (no unbound variables);
> what are the snapshot/restore boundary and cost; do unify and defeq share one budget or have
> separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for subtyping/Any/Never;
> defeq decides only equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional subtyping must not
> be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and production call graph before
> writing code**; 6.9.3c’s wiring contract has wasted two rounds by assuming that `can_assign` is
> the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instances.

> **E Acceptance and Residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① corpus/IR snapshot
> zero drift or itemized classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected integration tests; ③
> idempotent error-code generation (if an emission point/code table changes); ④ behavioral changes
> classified under D59 and made red before green. **Wiring tasks additionally require**: production
> call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many paths, which are reachable); using
> unit-test reachability as a substitute for user reachability is forbidden; rollback and budget
> must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537 (class D, proof-function formal
> refinement silently discarded; do not fix before adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on
> its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; C-stage boundary; if not closed, 6.9.4 covers only
> intra-module code), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14:
> orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see
> the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—three locations moved together on 2026-11-16:
> `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` are covered
> through the single rewrite target `rewritten_call_target` for `Call`/`TailCall`, and the init
> section and function body share one site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three mutations),
> #542 (orphaned shared layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two-entry-point
> wiring + removal of the C2c temporary workaround; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution
> and deviations), #552 (importing multi-parameter predicates and proof execution; adjacent to
> 6.9.5, separate case). **Ownership pending adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires
> (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equality bridge;
> decide whether they remain in 6.9.4 outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim complete Π/Σ; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does not
> fulfill open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwires; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is outside
> this item (E1002); witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 only
> cover forms that do not depend on proof-function formal refinement; if #539 is not fixed, 6.9.4
> covers only intra-module code; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 has landed (2026-11-19); the
> inner-isolation red state in 2.1.4 was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten by slot
> identity in the 2.1.4 closure) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a gate have been
> removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**revised on 2026-10-27, following the 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Directly driven test files** under `tests/` (tests that drive the changed code, such as
`tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change, but
**file / line count / reason must be registered for each item**; **tests must not be deleted and
assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic codes + baseline updates), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate adjudicated round.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criterion (2026-10-26 decision ②) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-difference requirement to the entire
> `tests/` directory. The revised criterion **changes only directly driven test files from “zero
> difference” to “may be modified, but file / line count / reason must be registered”**; the
> zero-difference requirements for the **corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer
> (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`)** remain unchanged. First application =
> 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, by **3 lines** (2 × `assert_format_eq`’s
> `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), because the changed spelling requires the expected type name in
> that assertion to be synchronized; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6
> 6.1 Name Canonicalization Closure.”

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and missing a consumer will **silently change
associativity** (no error, only a changed parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; every new operator must enter both the
table and the cross-validation test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 in `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code references `sema` in reverse, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness vulnerabilities must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x is exactly the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | The vulnerability criteria must be **written red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order would cause bugs to be frozen into the phase table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g’s (#399) deletion surface covers the rewriting targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the inventory is in this document’s §P3.5)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactoring and checker decomposition modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise, regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **P7 gate = the phase A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and 6.9.4 complete), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface, but must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume an undecided defeq/quantifier interface |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The final form of 9.5’s snapshot baseline and 9.3’s `pub(crate)` leak count can only be taken after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                  | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                |
| B                                      | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert by file                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| C                                      | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D                                      | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| E                                      | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All become mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| F                                      | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 can be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| G                                      | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch of files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal document constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move batch preceding P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc inspection,” while rules
  are “pre-work judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching something that should be
  refactored”; only the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 as the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the three concurrent inventories from
  original gap G3 made closure impossible. This table merges them so that 10 active scripts each
  belong to one phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and
  hard-conversion timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to be done after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewriting surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8
  (RFC-039 D56). Deferring it until after the refactoring means repeating the same batch of
  deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as
  incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and correcting RFC statuses into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker decomposition would exceed a revertible granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as hard acceptance**—the decomposition must be independently
  revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says that “the fixed
  defects should not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as a retrospective bisect marker.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renamed references; missing one **silently
  changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, and the deletion
  action remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to “independent issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left as an implementation remnant.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                           | **Revive it** (the prerequisite for P1 is that the revived tests contain genuine assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                           |
| C2              | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs. table-driven implementation                         | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + cross-validation of the two `BinOp` implementations from one source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 belongs to C6** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                         |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` allowlist                                        | **No allowlist**; the set difference must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                      |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 lists it as a mandatory verification item**; verify line by line during implementation                                                                                       |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                                 | **Merge the wasm-path vulnerability fix into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                       |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assign to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                                    |
| C8              | Correction of `upvalue_count` and the `.42` version number                          | **Fix it + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                                                |
